/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 22 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2991 (27)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4954 (120)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2223 (-53)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1567 (-4)
Baltic Handysize Index: 843 (-3)
CAPESIZE
The market ended the week on a firmer overall footing, with continued strength in the Pacific once again offsetting the more subdued sentiment seen across the Atlantic basin. The BCI 182 5TC rose by $1,093 to settle at $44,931, supported primarily by sustained Pacific activity and another active day from the major miners on C5. All three key miners were reportedly in the market today, reinforcing the Pacific as the clear source of support as the week drew to a close. C5 continued its upward trajectory, with the index gaining $0.360 to $15.625, while C3 remained largely rangebound with only a marginal increase of $0.091 to $36.241. Pacific volumes remained healthy throughout the session, continuing the strong fixing momentum witnessed across the week. Early C5 fixtures emerged around the $15.50-$15.60 level from miners, before a late operator fixture concluded at $15.75, helping sentiment finish on a stronger note into the weekend. In contrast, Atlantic activity remained comparatively muted. In the North Atlantic there was talk of improved offers circulating, though little concrete fixing activity materialised. On C3, activity remained limited, mirroring much of the week’s tone, with bids reported around the $36 to low-$36s range against owners maintaining offers closer to $37.
PANAMAX
As expected, the week closed on a softening note across both the Atlantic and Pacific basins, with the BPI time charter average falling by $481 to $20,004. Activity in the Atlantic was subdued, and overall sentiment remains weak, with the market still searching for a floor and further pressure on rates likely in the near term. The Pacific also stayed soft, as the growing influx of fresh tonnage continues to weigh heavily on sentiment. Unless there is a meaningful increase in cargo activity, the current bearish tone is expected to persist. The KM Singapore (80,599 2013) was reported fixed for trip delivery Butterworth 24/25 May via Indonesia to redelivery South China with coal at $23,000, although further details were not disclosed.
SUPRAMAX
With the long weekend coming up for a few, it was a rather inauspicious end to the week. Fundamentals changed little in the Atlantic and most players happy to wait until next week before committing. Both the US Gulf and South America remained finely balanced. From Asia it was another subdued day with the continued lack of fresh enquiry putting downward pressure on rates across most areas. The 11TC average finished the week down $62 at $19,801.

Atlantic
The Golden Sakura (63,425 2023) open Barranquilla 4 June was heard to have been placed on subjects basis delivery North Brazil for a trip China at around $18,500 plus $850,000 ballast bonus but no more details came to light. Also, the Port Orient (61,485 2017) open SW Pass was on subjects for a trip with grains to Spain at $27,000 to Cefetra. The Ocean Royal (58,110 2012dwt) open PT Cortes was likewise placed on subjects for trip with grains delivery SW Pass to NC South America at $20,000 to Norden. The MH Adagio (61,602 2022) open Tampa was on subjects for trip with coal basis SW Pass to Egypt at $31,000 with Oldendorff.

Asia
The Lilas Shine (61684 2011) ex dd at Zhoushan 24/25 May was heard fixed to Croatia at $23,000. Otherwise, little fresh activity surfaced.
HANDYSIZE
The week closed on a softer note, with the BHSI easing by 3 points to settle at 843, while the 7TC finished the week at $15,168. Activity in both the Continent and Mediterranean remained subdued, with most participants holding a positional stance and rates showing little movement. The South Atlantic also continued to soften, with rates still under pressure. The Kaszuby (38,980 2008) open Rio Grande was reportedly fixed for a trip from Up River in early June to the Caribbean at around $17,000–$18,000 by Bergebulk, although further details were not disclosed. The Norse Zealand (39,545 2025) open Douala was fixed on voyage terms from Up River to the West Mediterranean, again with no further details available. In the US Gulf, the ample supply of tonnage across most loading areas prevented any meaningful rate improvement. In Asia, the market remained flat, with sentiment continuing to appear largely positional. On the period side, the Stellar Trader (35,946 2013) open in Maracaibo reported fixed at high $13,000s for 4/6 months period by Cargill, but further details were not confirmed.

Market Fundamentals
US Weekly Grain Exports

In the week to 14 May, US combined exports of corn, wheat, soy (beans and meal) and sorghum dipped 0.4 Mt from the prior week to 2.7 Mt, USDA data show. This came as shipments declined of corn (-0.2 Mt to 1.4 Mt) and wheat (-0.2 Mt to 0.2 Mt). However, exports of soy (beans+meal) remained flat at 0.9 Mt while sorghum shipments edged 0.1 Mt higher to 0.2 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher in response to stronger C5 fixtures being done up to $15.60, in addition to bullish C3 fixtures being reported during the afternoon session. May was more stable today as we approach month end, rangebound trading between 41750 and 41900. June made the biggest gains with 38600 paid, followed by Jul contract with 34500 trading. The Jun v Jul spread widened and strengthened up to a high of 4300 in good volume. Q3 was actively trading 33200-33500 and the Q4 up to 32300, with the Q3 v Q4 spread trading above 1100. The Cals were pretty illiquid with no prints today on the Cal27 and just a single clip going through on the Cal28 at 23050.

PMX
PMX paper pushed higher across the curve today with the strength being lead by the front months. Jun traded from a low of 20000 up to 20750 before closing around 20650, seeing most of the volume between 20300–20600. Jul followed the same direction, trading from 20100 to 21000. Good size printed throughout the day with repeated selling at 21000. Q3 traded actively in a 19800–20250 range improving steadily throughout the session. Large clips traded at 20250. Q4 also improved, moving from 18600 to 18950 in lighter volumes. Further out, Cal 27 traded between 15350 and 15450.

INDEX (THURSDAY -1027 AND FRIDAY -631), AS MARKET CONTINUES TO FALL IN CHARTERERS FAVOUR. DEMAND CONTINUES TO BE LARGELY CONCENTRATED AROUND MID TO LATE JUNE DATES, PARTICULARLY FOR GRAIN BUSINESS. THE NORTH IS STILL OVER SUPPLIED SO ANY VESSELS THAT DO HAVE TO FIND COVER ARE FINDING IT HARD TO JUSTIFY THE OFFERS THAT WERE BEING ASKED EARLY IN THE WEEK, WHICH WERE AROUND 23K BKI CJK. NOPAC GRAIN TRIPS ARE NOW FIXING MID-HIGH USD 20K BKI CJK, REFLECTING THE SOFTER TONE IN THIS MARKET. WHILE E.AUS AND W.AUS PROVIDED EARLY SUPPORT THROUGH MINERAL, GRAINS AND ALUMINA ENQUIRY, THE GROWING TONNAGE LIST SHIFTED TRADING LEVERAGE TOWARD CHARTERERS. OWNERS INITIALLY REMAINED FIRM ON OFFERS, THOUGH AS NEGATIVE SENTIMENT PREVAILED, THEY WERE FORCED TO REDUCE THEIR IDEAS IN ORDER TO SECURE BUSINESS. IT IS ALSO WORTH NOTING THAT MULTIPLE VESSELS WERE FAILED ON AUS RV CARGOES, ADDING TO THE ALREADY OVERSUPPLIED SOUTH. AUS RV SPREADS ARE NOW 19.5K VS 21.5K BKI CJK, WITH FIXING VALUE NOW MID USD 20K BKI CJK, MARKING A CLEAR ADJUSTMENT FROM THE STRONGER IDEAS CIRCULATING AT THE BEGINNING OF THE WEEK WHERE OWNERS WERE AT USD 24K AND CHARTERERS 22K (BKI CJK). CURRENT INDO ROUNDS ARE NOW BEING FIXED AT MID USD 19K BKI HONG KONG FOR KMX AND MID USD 18K BKI HONG KONG FOR LMES. PROMPT DEMAND FOR INDO COAL ROUNDS CONTINUED TO EMERGE AS WELL AS SOME DEMAND FOR COAL EX INDO INTO INDIA, BUT ON THE WHOLE IT HAS NOT BEEN SUFFICIENT TO ABSORB THE GROWING SUPPLY IN THE SOUTH. THERE IS ALSO UNDERLYING UNCERTAINTY IN THE INDO COAL MARKET WITH REPORTS EARLY IN THE WEEK ABOUT A SHIFT IN INDO EXPORT POLICIES WEIGHING ON SENTIMENT AND CREATING A MORE CAUTIOUS TRADING ENVIRONMENT. ULTIMATELY THE PACIFIC MARKET TRADED ON A DOWNWARD TRAJECTORY THROUGHOUT THE WEEK. A HANDFUL OF FAILED SHIPS IS EVIDENT OF THE NEGATIVE SENTIMENT AND AS WE MOVE INTO NEXT WEEK IT IS CLEAR THERE IS A MORE FAVOURABLE MARKET FOR CHARTERERS IN THE NEAR-TERM. MUCH WILL DEPEND ON WHETHER FRESH CARGO DEMAND RETURNS EARLY NEXT WEEK, PARTICULARLY FROM COAL, THOUGH FOR NOW THE MARKET APPEARS LIKELY TO OPEN ON A SOFTER FOOTING. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场分化明显,Capesize凭借太平洋强劲需求持续走强(BCI+120至4954),而Panamax受制于运力过剩全线下滑(BPI-53至2223)。Baltic干散指数微涨27点至2991,但后市预期分歧,Capesize远期曲线显示Q3下跌而Panamax近月相对坚挺。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize市场由太平洋主导,三大矿商积极拿船,C5航线涨至15.625美元。西澳至中国航线活跃,6月船期紧张。Panamax则面临大西洋和太平洋双重压力,印尼煤炭需求不足以消化新增运力,租家有议价优势。Supramax和Handysize维持平稳偏弱格局。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 看多信号:Capesize现货大幅上涨1093美元至44931,5月前高位;C3保持36美元以上支撑,矿商活跃。看空信号:Panamax BPI单日跌481美元,P5航线周跌1047美元创新低;FFA曲线前端虽强但Q4预期已转弱,市场寻找底部。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 跨太平洋Capesize期租机会(6月FFA在38400-38600);关注Panamax 82K船型运力消化节奏,短期偏空但注意超跌反弹风险;Supramax 11TC 19,800一线支撑,基本面缺乏催化剂。关注印尼煤炭出口政策变化对市场情绪影响。
